label: lem:dynamics
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Exact highest-zero identity

title: Proof
body_md:
Implicit differentiation of \(H_t(z_0(t))=0\) gives
\(z_0'=H_t''(z_0)/H_t'(z_0)\).
The canonical-product zero-motion identity gives twice the regular
zero sum at \(z_0\); any real constant in the logarithmic derivative
has no imaginary contribution. The own conjugate contributes
\(2/(z_0-\bar z_0)=-i/y\).
An additional conjugate pair contributes
\(-2K_y(x-a,b)\) to \(y'\), and a real zero contributes half
this expression with \(b=0\).
Multiplication by \(2y\) proves \eqref{eq:dynamics}.
Absolute convergence of the imaginary parts follows from the paired
product representation and the zero-counting estimate; the summands
at large real abscissa are \(O(y/|a|^2)\).
Every numerator in \eqref{eq:K} is nonnegative when \(b\le y\).
The zero-motion and product framework is the one in
\cite{polymath,raymondfoundations}.

label: prop:rate
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Complete source to contraction rate

title: Proof
body_md:
Sum \eqref{eq:kernelineq} over all pairs except the own pair.
Equations \eqref{eq:dynamics} and \eqref{eq:S} give
\[
 q'\le-2-\frac{2\lambda}{h}q
          \left(\bar S_{t,h,r}(x)-\frac{s_r(q/h^2)}h\right).
 \]
Use the complete source floor and the whole-range cap.

title: Proof
body_md:
Proposition~\ref{prop:refinedsources} converts the complete
model-to-function premise (A1) and the finite tail certificate into
the refined source inequalities consumed below.
Construct the piecewise exact boundary \(\sqrt{\mathcal F_c(q,u)}\),
with upward restarts \eqref{eq:restart}.
It is initially strictly above all zeros by \eqref{eq:initial}.
Suppose a first positive contact occurs on a decreasing segment.
Premise (A3) localises the contact to a finite abscissa.
Premise (A2) and symmetry place an upper-right contact at \(x>X\).

At a multiple nonreal contact, backward Hermite splitting produces
an upward displacement of order \(\sqrt{\varepsilon}\) at time \(t-\varepsilon\).
The positive smooth comparison boundary changes by \(O(\varepsilon)\).
This contradicts the definition of first contact.
At a simple contact, \eqref{eq:eligible} ensures that the entire
kernel domain applies. Premise (A1) and
Proposition~\ref{prop:rate} give \(q'<-2-cq\), whereas the
comparison segment has derivative \(-2-cq\).
A zero branch reaching the boundary from below has the opposite
one-sided derivative requirement, a contradiction.
At a knot, the left segment suffices and the upward restart preserves
separation.

Thus all zeros remain below the comparison strip until its squared
height reaches \(q_{\mathrm e}\). Equations \eqref{eq:terminal}--\eqref{eq:ceiling}
and de Bruijn contraction give \(\Lambda\le U\).
The separately audited history evaluates
\(U=148611789321711/10^{15}\), as detailed below.

label: lem:positive
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:positive}
For \(t\ge0\), \(c_t(n)\) and \(\widetilde d_t(n)\) are nonnegative,
as are their time derivatives.
Moreover \(c_t(1)=1\), and
\(c_t(p)=\widetilde d_t(p)=0\) for \(p=2,3,5\).
head: environment
name: Positive finite coefficients

title: Proof
body_md:
Write \(d_t=\mathcal D\log_*b_t\). The derivation rule for
\(\mathcal D\), together with \(\partial_tb_t=\mathcal D^2b_t/4\),
gives
\[
 \partial_td_t(n)=\frac{\log^2n}{4}d_t(n)
       +\frac{\log n}{4}
          \sum_{\substack{ab=n\\a,b\ge2}}d_t(a)d_t(b).
\]
At \(t=0\), \(d_0\) is the nonnegative von Mangoldt sequence.
Induction on \(n\), followed by the integrating-factor formula,
proves positivity, including all time derivatives.
At a selected prime power \(p^k\), put
\(\kappa_p=(\log p)^2/4\) and
\(e_k=d_t(p^k)-(\log p)\mathrm e^{k\kappa_pt}\).
For \(k\ge2\),
\[
 e_k'=k^2\kappa_pe_k+
       (k^2-k)\kappa_p(\log p)\mathrm e^{k\kappa_pt}
       +\frac{k\log p}{4}
                 \sum_{j=1}^{k-1}d_t(p^j)d_t(p^{k-j}),\quad e_k(0)=0.
\]
The forcing and all its derivatives are nonnegative.
For \(k=1\), the residual is identically zero.
Elsewhere \(\widetilde d_t=d_t\).
Finally,
\[
 (\log n)c_t(n)=
       \sum_{\substack{d\mid n\\d\ge2}}\widetilde d_t(d)c_t(n/d)
\]
proves the claims for \(c_t\) by induction.

label: prop:tail
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Matched centred-tail transfer

title: Proof
body_md:
Use the exact identity
\[
 QT-V=(Q_0T-V_0)+(T-\nu)R-E.
\]
Since \(|T|\le D_K\) and \(|Q|\ge g\), a nonnegative residual
budget is
\[
 U_0=\bar B_0-(1-\bar A_0)D_K-2Z_J+(D_K+\nu)\eta+\varepsilon.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Re}(V/Q)\le\operatorname{Re} T+U_0/g\).
The cancellation
\[
 D_K+U_0/g=\frac{\bar B_0+\nu\eta+\varepsilon-2Z_J}{g}
\]
gives \eqref{eq:tailbound}.

label: rem:net
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:net}
At a fixed physical height, compare the complete quotient
\[
 \frac{\bar B_0+\nu\eta+\varepsilon-2Z_{J,\mathrm{low}}}
      {1-\bar A_0-\eta}
 \quad\text{with}\quad
 \frac{\bar B-2Z_{\mathrm{full,low}}}{1-\bar A},
\]
with the physical errors and paired phase deficits fully accounted
for in each candidate. Removing a tail loses some overlap credit.
Smaller \(\eta,\varepsilon\) alone therefore do not prove a larger source floor.
A complete old estimate can remain a fallback. Pointwise maxima
of valid complete candidates are taken before minima over the
source-class pairs.

name: Net improvement criterion

label: lem:cone
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:cone}
Assume \(0<C'\le C\) and \(\nu\ge2C'\). The complete cone at
the new parameter \(C'\)
is bounded below by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:newcone}
 C'(1+A_0+\eta)^2
  -(1+A_0+\eta)(B_0+\nu\eta+\varepsilon)-D
  +\mathcal P_{\rm retained}(C'),
\end{equation}
where \(\mathcal P_{\rm retained}(C')\) is the sum of the licensed,
nonnegative retained phase surpluses. The old debit \(D\) remains valid
if \(C'\le C\).
head: environment
name: Centred cone transfer

title: Proof
body_md:
For the core, expand \(C'|Q_0|^2-\operatorname{Re}(V_0\overline{Q_0})\)
about the aligned phases. Its constant/head surplus is
\((\omega_j-2C')a_j(1-\operatorname{Re} z_j)\); its unordered head/head surplus is
\((\omega_j+\omega_k-2C')a_ja_k(1-\operatorname{Re}(z_j\overline{z_k}))\).
For a negative frequency coefficient \(-b\), charging \(2b\) times
its label mass leaves the nonnegative surplus \(b(1+\cos\theta)\)
times that mass. For a positive coefficient, the surplus is
\(b(1-\cos\theta)\). This treats both retained chiralities.
Decreasing \(C\) decreases every exceptional magnitude, so the old
debit covers the new exceptional charges with nonnegative spare margin.
Omitted nonnegative surpluses may be discarded.

The difference between the full cone and the core cone is
\[
 \operatorname{Re}\bigl((2C'-\nu)R\overline{Q_0}-V_0\overline R\bigr)
 +(C'-\nu)|R|^2-\operatorname{Re}\bigl(E(\overline{Q_0}+\overline R)\bigr).
\]
It is at least
\[
 -\bigl((\nu-2C')(1+A_0)+B_0\bigr)\eta
 -(\nu-C')\eta^2-\varepsilon(1+A_0+\eta).
\]
Combining this with the core aligned-phase baseline gives
\eqref{eq:newcone} by direct expansion.

label: prop:prefix
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:prefix}
Suppose \(\mathcal B(u)\) bounds every twisted prefix
\(\bigl|\sum_{J<n\le u}\mathrm e^{2\pi if_j(n)}\bigr|\), uniformly
on the full source rectangle and for every \(0\le j<30\).
For continuously differentiable weights \(W_j\),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prefix}
 \left|\sum_{J<n\le M}W_j(n)\mathrm e^{2\pi if_j(n)}\right|
 \le |W_j(M)|\mathcal B(M)
       +\int_J^M\mathcal B(u)|W_j'(u)|\,\mathrm d u .
\end{equation}
Apply this to
\[
 W_j(u)=\mathrm e^{t(\log u)^2/4-\sigma\log u}F_j(\log u;t),
 \qquad (\log u-\nu)W_j(u),
 \quad \sigma=(1+h)/2+tL/4.
\]
The sum of the thirty resulting bounds supplies
\(\eta\) and \(\varepsilon\) in \eqref{eq:decomposition} for the removed
first-head tail.
head: environment
name: Uniform weighted-prefix transfer

title: Proof
body_md:
Discrete partial summation gives the endpoint term minus the
integral against the prefix step function. Taking absolute values
proves \eqref{eq:prefix}; the centred weight proves the moment
assertion. The coefficient identity \eqref{eq:fourier} is exact.

label: prop:refinedsources
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:refinedsources}
Under the complete model-to-function correspondence in (A1), the
uniform tail enclosures and rational checks described here give
\[
 \bar S_{t,h_{p,i},r}(x)>\ell^{\mathrm W}_{p,i,r}
       \quad(t\in I_i,\ x\ge X)
\]
for every provider, cell and declared fixed shift.
The schedules, observation heights, kernel domains and original
physical error allowances are unchanged.
head: environment
name: Complete refined providers

title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma~\ref{lem:cone}, the positive cone reserve in \eqref{eq:delta},
and the complete bounds \(A_*\le A^+\), \(B_*\le B^+\) license the
individual source increase \(\Delta/2\) with the original physical
perturbation charge. At a pair of translated observations this gives
\(\Delta/2\) in case \((0,0)\) and \(\Delta/4\) in case \((0,1)\).
The loss allowance \eqref{eq:creditloss} pays for both retained
surplus chiralities. The other nine case bounds are complete original
bounds. Their full minimum therefore applies at every physical centre,
including transitions between adjacent classes. Downward rounding
preserves the lower bound. The maximum with the original complete
floor is legitimate because both candidates hold on the entire domain.
Outside the refined cells the original complete estimate applies,
including its unbounded class and all future activations.
